FL-002.label: Memory units have a length cap; a memory over the cap is shortened to fit as one memory, and it is split only when it holds more than one distinct fact, with the split logged.
FL-002.walk: Save an over-cap single fact: shorten it into one memory, preserving its schedule and qualifiers; split only independent claims. Repeat the scout's long single-fact and two-fact inputs three times. The same prompt repairs failed checks up to three rounds; nothing is dropped silently and the original stays in the journal (M5RM / F208).
FL-002.observed: A two-fact request saved two linked children and reinforced both on repetition. The three-pass over-cap shortening series was not collected. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-014.label: Every memory records the folder the agent stood in when it was made.
FL-014.walk: `/remember` while the agent stands in a folder; the card shows that folder as WHERE.
FL-014.observed: The saved museum fact showed the packet project directory in WHERE and PROJECT.

FL-038.label: A cheap 80/20 duplicate check at memory creation, keeping the agent's memory work under 10% of build run time.
FL-038.walk: Save a fact already in the Palace: at cosine 0.92 or above the save comes back 'already known — reinforced' at once, between 0.80 and 0.92 it asks to confirm, without the agent reading other memories; these write-time bands are the C.4 defaults and are separate from the curator's own search band (v2.128).
FL-038.observed: Resending the identical orchard fact reinforced it. A rewording of the Willow Pier example scored 0.815 and offered the explicit save-anyway choice. No override was sent.

FL-042.label: Constitution: 'Already known — reinforced' on re-saves; rejected candidates remembered and never re-proposed without material change (gate-day).
FL-042.walk: Re-save a known fact; the reply says 'already known — reinforced'; reject a candidate and re-save it unchanged; it is not proposed again.
FL-042.observed: The exact repeat reinforced the same memory. The rejected-candidate re-save portion was not exercised. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-069.label: The core tools every modern harness has: files, terminal, Chrome, skills, changing models, compaction (our own take), and interactions with common apps, taken from the most modular standard source.
FL-069.walk: Ask the agent to read a file, run a terminal command, open a page in the browser and use a skill; each works.
FL-069.observed: Opened the thread tool inventory. A file, terminal, browser and skill sequence through an agent was not walked. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-187.label: Two repos, the spine (memory) and the Harness, not a mono repo.
FL-187.walk: List the repositories; the spine and the Harness are two separate git repos.
FL-187.observed: Verified distinct Git roots and origin URLs for nocturne-harness and nocturne-memory and built one wheel from each. The screenshot shows the installed pair in operation.

FL-190.label: The Harness can use skills and has the best and most common tools available, compiled from a list.
FL-190.walk: Ask the agent to use a skill in a thread; it loads the skill and follows it.
FL-190.observed: The tool inventory opened. A model-driven skill invocation was not verified. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-191.label: The tools and skills Claude Code and Codex use on this machine, pinned to versioned open-source sources.
FL-191.walk: Open the tool inventory; each tool or skill lists the versioned open-source source it is pinned to.
FL-191.observed: The inventory opened but the default Stage clipped much of its panel. Every source and version was not verified. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-194.label: The Pydantic toolset and skills as the tool layer.
FL-194.walk: Open the agent's tool list in a thread; the tools come from the Pydantic toolset plus skills, not from pi.
FL-194.observed: Opened the real thread tool inventory. The clipped view did not prove the provenance of every entry. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-006.label: Every memory carries a location column and a project column.
FL-006.walk: Move between two folders inside one thread, say a fact in each, then compact: each memory born carries the location of the message it came from (the folder the agent stood in when the fact was said), not the folder at compaction time; the memory card and the palace column show it (SD-072).
FL-006.observed: The explicit save carried its working folder. Two locations followed by compaction were not exercised. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-007.label: Every memory links to the full conversation it came from, so an agent can reach more than just the memory when needed.
FL-007.walk: Open a memory card; it names the conversation it came from, and following that link opens the conversation.
FL-007.observed: Opened the origin-thread control while that thread was already selected. The card names the origin but this did not establish navigation from a different conversation. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-009.label: Record files (history, transcripts) live apart from code so code can be deleted and re-downloaded without losing history.
FL-009.walk: Delete the code folder, reinstall, `nocturne up`; every thread is still there.
FL-009.observed: Installing local wheels against the existing verification home retained the thread and memories. Deleting a checkout was not part of this walk. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-010.label: Every thread has a thread id, and every memory records the thread it was born in.
FL-010.walk: Open a memory card; the thread it was born in is named.
FL-010.observed: The museum memory showed its originating New thread in provenance. Its r2 history retained the initial save and the reinforcement.

FL-061.label: Compaction instructions tuned by back-test; memory size as a tunable beside the threshold and allotments.
FL-061.walk: In the Injection Console, change Memory size to back-test and inspect the joint replay with minimum match and memory share. Instruction generations retain text, parent, date, size and scores. A winning production fit carries instructions and size in the scorer proposal and its existing activation; previews retain only a receipt. Verification feedback is excluded from production training.
FL-061.observed: Explicit memories were saved on a verification principal. Scorer back-tests and production activation require separate coverage. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-080.label: Compaction triggered by fill percentage against the model's best working range and max, which vary by model.
FL-080.walk: Fill a thread past its model's fill line; compaction runs and the fill percentage drops.
FL-080.observed: Two explicit facts were split. Filling a thread through its compaction threshold was not walked. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-084.label: Plan-mode compaction: the summarizer asks the user one to four questions before compacting. (seed SD-040)
FL-084.walk: Enable /compact plan on, cross the configured fill line, and answer the one to four model questions. No history is dropped before the answer; the ensuing compaction record retains questions and answer, including across restart.
FL-084.observed: The split preserved the explicit source. Interactive plan-mode compaction across restart was not exercised. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-170.label: A fresh reinstall that reconnects to existing files and auto-finds the cloud palace.
FL-170.walk: Reinstall on the same machine and run the start command; it finds the existing cloud Palace and the old threads without being told where they are.
FL-170.observed: The local wheel installation reconnected to the existing local verification home. The charge requires a local Palace and excludes owner cloud discovery. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-186.label: Build on Pydantic AI in a way that lets us modify and extend without waiting on them, passing features back and forth with their library.
FL-186.walk: Upgrade the Pydantic AI dependency; the Harness's own additions keep working and the new upstream features are usable.
FL-186.observed: The lockfile-pinned dependencies ran the verification thread. Upgrading Pydantic AI changes a dependency outside this recipe. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-192.label: Swappable seams: router, model policy with an off-switch, toolset as a unit, memory system.
FL-192.walk: Change the toolset in config to a different one as a unit; the next thread's agent has that toolset's tools.
FL-192.observed: The walk used the installed default toolset. A switch of toolsets in a new thread was not verified. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.

FL-193.label: The common core of terminal-agent tools (skills, progressive prompting, model switching, compaction, app interactions) in one piece that pulls upstream updates.
FL-193.walk: Update the shared core-tools piece to its newest upstream version; skills, model switching and the rest keep working in the Harness.
FL-193.observed: The released core tools were used. Updating shared core tools to an upstream release changes dependencies outside this recipe. The capture is packet context for the missing proof.
